source: Hand-compiled from public shipping and trade summaries (UNCTAD, EIA, canal authorities); rounded
caveat: The lanes are the usual routes, not live ship positions. Volumes are rough, widely quoted figures.

routes.what: Containers and goods from China, Korea and Southeast Asia to Europe through the Red Sea and the Suez Canal.
Crude from Saudi Arabia, Iraq, the UAE and Kuwait to India, China, Japan and Korea, through the Strait of Hormuz.
Goods from East Asia to the US West Coast, one of the busiest container routes.

routes.n: Around the Cape of Good Hope
routes.what: The long way round Africa between Asia and the Atlantic. Used by ships too big for Suez or avoiding it.
Goods, fuel and machinery between Europe and North America.

routes.n: US East Coast to Panama and the Pacific
routes.what: Ships between the Atlantic and Pacific use the Panama Canal; goods head on to Asia.
From the Pacific end of the Panama Canal across the ocean to East Asia.
Iron ore and soybeans from Brazil to China, around the Cape of Good Hope.
US crude, fuel and gas exports to Europe, now among the world's biggest.

routes.n: Black Sea grain to the Mediterranean
routes.what: Wheat, corn and sunflower oil from Ukraine, Russia and Romania via the Bosphorus.

chokes.note: About a fifth of the world's oil passes through this narrow gap at the mouth of the Persian Gulf.
The short cut between the Indian and Pacific oceans; one of the busiest lanes in the world, and narrow.
Cuts out the trip round Africa; roughly one in eight of the world's traded goods by value uses it, normally.
The gate between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Attacks on ships here since late 2023 pushed many round Africa instead.
Links the Atlantic and Pacific; around 5% of world sea trade, and sensitive to drought.
The entrance to the Mediterranean from the Atlantic.
The only way out of the Black Sea; grain and oil pass through the heart of Istanbul.
The route round Africa when Suez is closed or too small for the ship.
Much of the world's container traffic from East Asia passes through or beside it.
The busiest shipping lane in Europe, to the ports of Rotterdam, Antwerp and Hamburg.
